summary: Checks whether a value is **not** a sheet id.
description: `nonValidSheetId(value)` is the same test as `!isValidSheetId(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
Apps Script numbers its sheets from zero, so a sheet id is a non-negative safe integer — the same rule `isCountable` applies. The id of the first sheet in a spreadsheet is `0`.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not a sheet id; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonValidSheetId(-1); // => true
nonValidSheetId(1.5); // => true
nonValidSheetId("0"); // => true
nonValidSheetId(0); // => false
nonValidSheetId(1234567890); // => false
```
